problem_statement: SMBus drivers that lack hardware packet-error-checking need software routines to compute and verify the PEC byte. A routine must compute the PEC byte for a write transaction given a target 7-bit address and the I2C messages of the transaction (using CRC-8 CCITT over the address, direction, repeated-start, and data bytes), and a routine must verify a received PEC byte for read transactions (Read Byte, Read Word, Block Read), returning success when it matches the computed value and an error when it does not. These routines must only act when PEC is enabled for the transaction and must be available to drivers that enable software PEC support.
